name: Clingendael / Planetary Security Initiative
note: clingendael.org refused retrieval for a seventh consecutive week on 2026-10-25, so whether the institute published is unknown rather than negative — a hole in the observation, not a finding. The sister-site route was worked as instructed: planetarysecurityinitiative.org/news carried two items in the week, a commentary on climate and Indian warfare (posted 19 October) and an American institute's report on Gulf energy infrastructure (posted 23 October), both other institutions' work, so neither counts as the institute's output. Its head of EU and global affairs, Louise van Schaik, was on the Montreal summit speaker list. Team details as confirmed on 2026-09-27 stand. The last publicly datable funding phase for the platform is still December 2019.

name: HCSS
note: Still publishing, and not on climate. In the week to 2026-10-11 its output was a paper arguing Europe needs a credible alternative when the alliance cannot act (8 October), a policy brief on polysilicon supply chains by Ron Stoop and Irina Patrahau (6 October), and a podcast on Chinese development cooperation (5 October) co-hosted by Laura Birkman, director of its climate, water and food security programme. Under the split rule that is lead time from a research institute rather than a finding about priorities — but what it did publish is itself a priority signal, and it is raw materials and alliance contingency. One correction made 2026-10-11: the July 2026 analysis of the Dutch defence climate strategy is by Birkman, dated 15 July, not by another researcher on the 16th, and its load-bearing point is that the strategy has no plan for the climate, weather and ocean data infrastructure anticipation depends on.

name: KNMI
role: National meteorological institute; attribution capability, and now a seat in another state’s security machinery
note: Dutch researchers sit in the attribution network's Caribbean drought team. Added 2026-10-25: the institute's director-general, Maarten van Aalst — in post since 1 February 2023 by the institute's own board page, also its Chief Science Officer, previously head of the Red Cross Red Crescent Climate Centre — is one of sixteen members of the British climate and nature security taskforce whose membership was published on 21 October 2026. The first person responsible for an operational observing system to hold a formal seat in a national security-risk body, which is the configuration the radio-spectrum question has been waiting for.

name: Red Cross Red Crescent Climate Centre
note: Reporting on Caribbean drought-hit farmers.

name: World Weather Attribution
note: Re-checked 2026-10-25: the studies index still shows nothing after 28 August and the site's own most recent dated item is the 17 September Himalaya report, so the index is still not the whole output — check both. Nothing on the week's category-five Pacific typhoon, which would not be expected this soon. Under the rule corrected on 2026-09-20 that is evidence about how long the work takes and nothing else: the question to ask of an attribution network is whether it has declined a case it was asked to take, and nothing suggests it has.

name: adelphi
note: Correction, 2026-10-04, and it reverses what this file said for three weeks. The Berlin Climate and Security Conference does have a 2026 edition: 6 October 2026, hosted by the German Federal Foreign Office with adelphi, theme 'A climate for security, freedom and prosperity', in person by invitation and streamed, with side events alongside the Climate for Peace Initiative and the Climate Security Expert Network. Confirmed against the conference's own site, which is a different host from adelphi's publications index — and the three checks of that index that produced the earlier conclusion were one observation repeated, not three pieces of evidence. The rule that follows: for a dated fixture, score only a disconfirmation.

name: MERICS
note: 2022 analysis of China's refusal to securitise climate; no current replacement found.

name: SIPRI
note: Re-checked 2026-10-25, and this corrects the method rather than the fact. The climate-change-and-security publications list still ends at the August 2026 Abyei study, which would have been scored as a third month of lead time and would have been wrong: on 22 October the director of the institute's climate change and risk programme, Florian Krampe, published the week's sharpest institutional argument — that climate security has everyone's mandate and nobody's budget, that the threat-multiplier formulation names no mechanism, and that someone must own the gap between a forecast and the money — on a Washington research blog, with nothing about it on sipri.org. Check the people as well as the publications index. The Lake Chad climate, peace and security fact sheet of June 2026 is still unread.

name: NUPI
role: Training for Peace; climate and peacekeeping
note: Co-author of 'Beyond the blue line' on UNISFA.

name: Danish Refugee Council
note: Projected up to 3 million displaced by East African flooding.

name: NATO HQ / Science and Technology Organization
note: On 15 September 2026 NATO issued the 2026 Resilience Baseline Requirements, the first substantial revision of the seven baseline requirements since Warsaw 2016 and the first public release of them, announced 17 September. Extreme weather, natural disasters, space weather and changing environmental conditions appear among the cross-cutting risks; requirement 4 now obliges exercised contingency plans for food and water supply against all threats and hazards; the phrase 'climate change' appears nowhere in the document and the announcement mentions neither climate nor extreme weather. The Secretary-General's annual Climate Change and Security Impact Assessment is still listed for 2022, 2023 and 2024 with nothing since and no statement about it. Read official texts, not only the topic page: checking the topic page alone produced a wrong finding of silence in the week to 2026-09-20. SAS-182 (January 2026) is a research-task-group output and does not substitute.

name: EEAS
note: The climate-and-security nexus page is stale to 28 June 2023, but the service itself moved on 24 September 2026: High Representative and Commission Vice-President Kaja Kallas co-hosted a UNGA foreign ministers' dialogue on climate change and ecosystem degradation as national security risks with the UK and Kenya, and the service published the co-hosts' statement. That is the Union's security principal using this field's own register rather than an economic-security substitute, and it is the first such instance in this record.

name: IMCCS / Council on Strategic Risks / Center for Climate and Security
note: Checked 2026-10-11 on councilonstrategicrisks.org, not on the old climateandsecurity.org domain. No climate research published in the week: a September media round-up (9 October) and an event recap of New York Climate Week and the General Assembly (6 October). What the parent organisation launched was a second cohort of an AI and National Security Convergence Fellowship, applications open 5 October and due 20 October. Three consecutive weeks with no state-level climate briefer since Ohio on 18 September, and no state government ever named as commissioner or partner on any of the five. The institute's private tabletop with a solar-geoengineering research organisation on a fictional 2030 stratospheric aerosol deployment runs 14 October, unminuted and with no participants named. The military council it houses has been silent for twelve months: no World Climate and Security Report since 2024 and no item of any kind since an open letter of 23 October 2025.

name: UN Climate Security Mechanism
role: DPPA / UNDP / UNEP / DPO joint programme
note: Phase III extended to run 2026-2028, with ten advisers deployed to UN missions and regional organisations — the most recent a climate, peace and security adviser to the Pacific Islands Forum, onboarded June 2026 — and fourteen contributing governments as of January 2026, funded through a UN multi-partner trust fund. The UK added £1 million on 25 September 2026, three tenths of one per cent of a £331 million package announced under the heading of climate-driven instability. Annual funding volumes are still unread: the trust fund lists a consolidated financial report for 2025 whose figures did not render on 2026-09-27.

name: Security Council Report
note: Tracks Council activity under a natural-resource governance frame.

name: UNEP
note: Published the Emissions Gap Report 2026, The Point of Return, on 21 October 2026, nineteen days before the Antalya conference: overshoot of 1.5C treated as virtually unavoidable, a lowest-overshoot peak of 1.7-1.8C around mid-century, about 2.8C under current policies. It completes the overshoot concession this routine first recorded in the programme's September spotlight report. Note two things for next time: none of the published readings record any treatment of adaptation, adaptation limits, loss and damage or security; and unep.org, its press releases and its document repository all refused retrieval on 2026-10-25, so the figures had to be taken from the UN news service and an independent analysis. Use those routes first.

name: ICIMOD
note: Called the Langtang-Lirung event an ice-and-rock avalanche cascade, not a GLOF, and on 11 September 2026 its Saswata Sanyal called hazard-specific disaster planning obsolete.

name: UNFCCC secretariat
note: Added 2026-09-13. Executive Secretary Simon Stiell argued climate as a 'continent-wide economic security emergency' to the European Parliament on 10 September — the economic register, not this field's. The US withdrew from the convention on 7 January 2026. Coordinate is the city of Bonn, not the UN Campus.

name: UK Climate and Nature Security Taskforce
role: The only standing national ministerial climate-security body in the field
note: Formally the National Security and Resilience Risks of a Changing Climate and Nature Loss Taskforce. Convened by the Department for Energy Security and Net Zero with the Cabinet Office; sixteen-member membership published 21 October 2026 and inaugural meeting held the same week, co-chaired by Katie White, Minister for Climate Transition, and Baroness Twycross. Its membership is the best public map of the field's usable expertise and much of it is not British: Erin Sikorsky of the Center for Climate and Security, Maarten van Aalst of the Royal Netherlands Meteorological Institute, Janani Vivekananda of adelphi, David Obura as IPBES chair, Comfort Ero of the International Crisis Group, Gen. Richard Nugee, and the Bank of England among others. Terms: identify key climate and nature risks to UK security and resilience, review and challenge the government's own work, recommend how to strengthen resilience and shape international outcomes. It has up to two meetings in 2026, no published reporting date, no budget and no measurable target. Score it on whether a recommendation of its reaches a spending document.

name: NATO Climate Change and Security Centre of Excellence
role: Alliance climate-security centre of excellence; a distinct body from NATO HQ and the Science and Technology Organization
note: Ten days after holding the fifth Montreal climate security summit on 15 and 16 October 2026 — Resilient Defence: Climate-Smart Investments on the Road to 5%, by invitation, nine tracks naming climate throughout — neither the centre nor its Canadian co-host had published any account of it. The centre's whole 2026 news stream is two items: a spring course in May and a welcome to its 2026 fellows on 6 October. The comparators found on 2026-10-25 make this a contrast rather than a silence: the 2024 edition produced a recap on 30 October 2024, the 2025 edition one on 15 October 2025, and the 2025 edition also produced a Canadian defence minister's speech published on canada.ca. Nothing equivalent exists for 2026. Watch for a climate-resilience metric for defence procurement, not for a communique.

name: ITU
role: Spectrum allocation; the forum in which the observing system's frequency bands are contested
note: Added 2026-10-04. On 28 September the ITU and WMO Secretaries-General, Doreen Bogdan-Martin and Celeste Saulo, issued a joint appeal to protect the radio-frequency bands weather and climate observation depends on — satellite sounding, weather radar, lightning location, aircraft and marine observations, hydrological monitoring — at a joint seminar in Geneva, 28 to 30 September, pointing at the 2027 World Radiocommunication Conference. Saulo's point is why it belongs here: the bands are fixed by atmospheric physics rather than chosen, so meteorology cannot trade out of them. Note the institutional coincidence: the ITU is also the COP31 presidency's partner on the Antalya artificial-intelligence pledge of 21 September.

name: FEWS NET
role: Famine early warning; produces the field's inputs rather than its arguments
note: Added 2026-10-11. The Famine Early Warning Systems Network published a global special report on the food security impacts of the 2026-27 El Niño on 6 October 2026, naming unimodal East Africa and Southern Africa at highest concern. In the week the strongest El Niño on record was put on the record, this network and three UN agencies made the argument and no ministry, alliance body or council said anything about it. Two findings in its own report cut against the alarm around it: global maize, wheat and rice output has changed little on balance across strong and very strong El Niño years, and the severe outcomes arrive in the following lean season rather than during the rains — which is the whole case for anticipatory action and the whole reason it keeps failing. Check the global special reports index and the country outlook pages separately.

name: WMO
role: World Meteorological Organization; the observing system, and host of the climate panel's secretariat
note: Added 2026-10-11 to close a drift: the standing roster has tracked the telecommunications union and the meteorological organization together since their joint appeal of 28 September 2026 on the radio-frequency bands weather and climate observation depends on, but only the union was on this layer. Celeste Saulo's formulation is the one to keep — the spectrum is a finite natural resource and meteorology relies on specific bands determined not by choice but by the physical properties of the atmosphere. Geneva is also where the climate panel's secretariat sits, which is where its 9 October 2026 advisory for the Addis Ababa plenary came from. Nothing from any defence ministry or alliance body has engaged the observing system as an asset to defend.

name: Anticipation Hub
role: Anticipatory action community of practice; holds the only public annual count of the field's central operational doctrine
note: Hosted by the German Red Cross with the international federation and the Red Cross Red Crescent climate centre as co-initiators, its coordination team drawn from all three and its primary office in Berlin. Added to the roster 2026-10-18 after its annual global overview was found to contain the anticipatory-disbursement figure this routine had reported for three weeks as not existing in public: for 2025, 146 activations across 54 countries, almost US$120 million released and 9.6 million people reached.

name: Conference of Defence Associations Institute
role: Canadian defence research institute; co-host of the Montreal climate security summit with the alliance's climate centre
note: Added to the roster 2026-10-18. Its published summit speaker list is currently the most complete public map of who works on defence and climate across the alliance, and is the route by which the 2026 edition's participation was established when neither host published an account of it. Treat titles on that list as the host's own rather than as verified: it gives the European external action service's climate envoy a role title no European source confirms.

name: Institute of Peace and Conflict Studies
role: Indian security research institute; the route into the Indian file this routine spent nine weeks failing to find
note: Director Ruhee Neog. Co-published Special Report 227, Shared Vulnerability, Divided Action: South Asia's Climate Paradox, with Clingendael on 12 October 2026, from a track 1.5 workshop at Kochi in May 2026. Its argument — that shared climate vulnerability in South Asia does not produce collective action, because governance stays national and siloed and proposals are designed for political feasibility rather than for the risk — is the best explanation this routine has found for the Indian file's emptiness. Naming trap: in these digests IPCS is this institute, IPCC is the climate panel and IPC is the food-security classification scale. Where to look: ipcs.org's issue listing.
